'''Rösti''' is a [[Cookbook:potato|potato]] dish from Switzerland. It was originally a common [[Cookbook:Breakfast|breakfast]] eaten by farmers in the canton of Bern, but today is eaten all over Switzerland. Many Swiss people consider rösti a national dish. Today it is more commonly served to accompany other dishes, rather than for breakfast. 

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Potato|potato]] (either washed or peeled)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]

==Procedure==
#[[Cookbook:Grating|Grate]] the potato into a dish, and squeeze out the excess moisture, discarding the liquid.
#Split the mixture into two even piles.
#Pour the oil into a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] and heat moderately.
#Place the two piles separately onto the pan, pushing down on top of them with a spatula in order to ensure that the piles stay intact.
#[[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] until the underside is golden brown, then carefully flip and cook the other side.
#Add salt and pepper to taste, and serve.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*There are many variations of rösti.
*Various rösti use [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]], [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], or [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]]. These can be mixed in with the potato before you start to fry the rösti.
*Generally, any dry ingredients you use should be grated or diced before being added to the mix.
*The outside of the rosti should be crisp. To achieve this the potato should be as dry as possible before it is fried.
